subject: Custody transfer orchestration & erase attestation — VPC private deployment
messages:
From: Tanya Ruiz <tanya.ruiz@medicahealth.com>

Date: 2029-04-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Data custody and verified deletion at contract termination

Hi Connor —

Hope you’re well. As we move toward our procurement close, our security team needs a clear, auditable process for what happens to tenant data in a Private/VPC deployment when the contract terminates or the tenant is decommissioned. Specifically we need to know:  

- The orchestration steps Redwood runs (or that we can run) to transfer custody or destroy customer-owned objects in the customer-controlled storage.  
- Evidence we can reasonably obtain that shows each step completed (logs, timestamps, signatures).  
- Typical timelines for a full verification (snapshot -> wipe -> audit).  
- Any escrow or third-party attestation options you offer if we require an independent cert.  

Can you share a concise checklist and example artifacts? We’ll need this for our legal/security review.

Thanks,
Tanya Ruiz
Director, Information Security
Medica Health

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Tanya Ruiz <tanya.ruiz@medicahealth.com>
Date: 2029-04-10T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data custody and verified deletion at contract termination

Tanya —

Thanks for the clear ask. High level answer before I gather the runbook:  

- For Private/VPC deployments where storage is customer-controlled (S3/GCS-like or customer-attached NVMe), the standard flow is a coordinated custody transfer: snapshot of final state -> delivery of an encrypted archive to customer-managed location (optional) -> cryptographic tombstone creation on control plane -> systematic overwrite/secure-delete of objects at storage tier -> KV cache and ephemeral artifacts scrubbed on GPU hosts.  

- Evidence we provide: per-step operation logs (job id, operator id, timestamps), signed MD5/SHA256 manifests for archived snapshots, and a post-wipe audit bundle (operation logs + sample delete confirmation entries).  

- Typical end-to-end timeline: most small tenants (<=1 TB) are verified within 48-72 hours; larger datasets depend on egress throughput and wipe policy (our default secure-delete runs at parallelized worker jobs). We’ll provide an estimate after we see the dataset size.  

- We can accommodate third-party attestation: Redwood works with accredited auditors for a scoped attestation engagement; timing and cost vary.

I’ll loop in our operations lead to provide the checklist and sample artifacts. One quick Q: do you expect Redwood to push a snapshot to your bucket, or will you pull? We can do either, but the coordination affects timeline and required IAM roles.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Hi all —

Attached are the detailed artifacts and a short checklist. Summaries below and attachments are: redwood_vpc_erase_runbook_v2.pdf and sample_erase-audit-log.txt (redacted).

Checklist (concise):
1) Pre-exit discovery (T-5 days): inventory of buckets/objects, size, versioning state, and any object locks/retention. Customer to provide the destination bucket + write creds.
2) Snapshot & manifest (T-3 days): create a compressed, encrypted snapshot of tenant data; compute SHA256 checksums for each object; operator creates signed manifest (operator id + timestamp, HMAC signature using operator KMS key). Deliver snapshot to customer bucket (push) and mark control-plane tombstone.
3) Verification window (T-2 to T): customer confirms receipt and checksum match. If they accept, Redwood schedules deletion jobs.
4) Deletion & overwrite (T to T+1): run parallelized secure-delete across storage endpoints; if object versioning present, iterate versions and tombstone immutability holds first (requires customer coordination). Logs capture job id, worker id, operator id, and per-object deletion events.
5) KV & ephemeral scrub (same window): clear model KV caches, ephemeral scratch on inference nodes, and zero-out crypto material per our crypto-sanitize policy.
6) Audit bundle delivery (T+1 to T+2): produce audit bundle (operation logs, manifest, signed operator statements) and deliver to customer bucket and to Redwood control plane archive for 30 days.

Notes on your questions:  
- Storage classes & retention: we respect server-side immutability/retention holds — if a bucket has an Object Lock policy, we surface that in pre-exit discovery and require Medica to lift holds or confirm desired policy. For GCS/Archival classes, secure-delete still runs but timelines increase due to retrieval times.
- Signed operator timestamps: our operator actions are recorded in an auditable event stream; each operator action includes a signed entry (operator id, cert fingerprint, ISO timestamp) and a KMS-backed HMAC. Sample entries are in sample_erase-audit-log.txt.
- Third-party attestation: we partner with two accredited firms for scoped attestations. Typical scope for a tenancy-level erase attestation is 2–3 weeks on-site/remote, and cost range is $18k–$35k depending on dataset complexity and scope.

Attachments referenced: redwood_vpc_erase_runbook_v2.pdf (runbook + checklist + roles matrix), sample_erase-audit-log.txt (redacted log snippets).

Action items for Medica:
- Share destination bucket ARN and short-lived write IAM role by EOD 2029-04-12.
- Confirm whether you will retain sealed snapshot (you said yes for 90d). If object locks exist, identify which buckets require owner action.

If acceptable, Connor and I will prepare an evidence bundle template you can drop into your legal review.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Operations, Private Deployments
